title: Primitive element in a nonzero kernel from a connected filtered coalgebra
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $C,D$ be $k$-vector spaces with linear maps $\Delta_C:C\to C\otimes_k C$, $\epsilon_C:C\to k$ and $\Delta_D:D\to D\otimes_k D$, $\epsilon_D:D\to k$. Tensor products have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Assume for $E=C,D$ the coalgebra identities
$$(\Delta_E\otimes1)\Delta_E=(1\otimes\Delta_E)\Delta_E,\qquad(\epsilon_E\otimes1)\Delta_E=(1\otimes\epsilon_E)\Delta_E=1_E$$
under the tensor associativity and unit identifications. Fix $g\in C$ with $\Delta_C(g)=g\otimes g$ and $\epsilon_C(g)=1$. Suppose there are increasing linear subspaces $C_0\subseteq C_1\subseteq\cdots$, with $C_0=kg$, $\bigcup_{n\ge0}C_n=C$, and
$$\Delta_C(C_n)\subseteq\sum_{i=0}^n C_i\otimes_k C_{n-i}.$$
Each tensor subspace denotes its image in $C\otimes_k C$. Let $f:C\to D$ be linear with $\Delta_Df=(f\otimes f)\Delta_C$ and $\epsilon_Df=\epsilon_C$. If $f$ is not injective, there is $x\ne0$ with
$$f(x)=0,\qquad\epsilon_C(x)=0,\qquad\Delta_C(x)=x\otimes g+g\otimes x.$$
Neither $C$ nor $D$ is assumed finite-dimensional; no algebra structure, cocommutativity, or characteristic hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 14.43, printed p.294, coproduct calculation, together with the connected filtration of Definition 14.4 and equation (91), printed p.281. The kernel-detection statement is an agent-written general coalgebra lemma using these structures, not a quotation of Lemma 14.44.

proof.text: Noninjectivity and linearity give a nonzero element of $\ker f$. By exhaustiveness, choose the least $n$ for which $C_n\cap\ker f\ne0$, and choose $0\ne x\in C_n\cap\ker f$. Counit preservation gives $\epsilon_C(x)=\epsilon_D(f(x))=0$. If $n=0$, write $x=ag$ and apply $\epsilon_C$ to obtain $a=0$, a contradiction. Thus $n\ge1$. Put $L=C_{n-1}$, with inclusion $\iota:L\to C$, and $h=f\iota:L\to D$. Minimality gives $\ker h=0$: an element of this kernel is an element of $C_{n-1}\cap\ker f$.

source.place: Definition 14.4 and equation (91), printed p.281; Lemma 14.43, printed p.294, coproduct calculation. Agent-written least-filtration-degree kernel argument.

proof.text:
Define the linear map $p:C\to C$ by $p(y)=y-\epsilon_C(y)g$. Since $\epsilon_C(g)=1$, $p$ kills $C_0=kg$ and preserves every $C_i$. Expanding on pure tensors, and using both counit identities, gives
$$(p\otimes p)\Delta_C(x)=\Delta_C(x)-g\otimes x-x\otimes g+\epsilon_C(x)g\otimes g=\Delta_C(x)-g\otimes x-x\otimes g=:r.$$
For each summand $C_i\otimes C_{n-i}$ of the filtration condition, applying $p\otimes p$ kills it when $i=0$ or $i=n$. For $0<i<n$, both $p(C_i)$ and $p(C_{n-i})$ lie in $L$. Expressing the finitely many tensor summands as sums of pure tensors therefore gives $t\in L\otimes_k L$ with $(\iota\otimes\iota)(t)=r$. This is an image statement and requires no injectivity of tensor subspace inclusions.

source.place: Definition 14.4 and equation (91), printed p.281; Lemma 14.43, printed p.294, coproduct calculation. Agent-written least-filtration-degree kernel argument.

proof.text:
The coalgebra-map identity and $f(x)=0$ give
$$(f\otimes f)(r)=\Delta_D(f(x))-f(g)\otimes f(x)-f(x)\otimes f(g)=0.$$
Functoriality of tensor maps, checked on their pure-tensor generators, consequently gives $(h\otimes h)(t)=0$ in $D\otimes_kD$.

source.place: Definition 14.4 and equation (91), printed p.281; Lemma 14.43, printed p.294, coproduct calculation. Agent-written least-filtration-degree kernel argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-vector-space-tensor-family-zero-detection] to the singleton family consisting of $h$, which detects zero by step 1. Write $s=(h\otimes1_L)(t)\in D\otimes_k L$. The equation from step 3 says $(1_D\otimes h)(s)=0$. The flip maps $\tau(u\otimes v)=v\otimes u$ exist by the tensor universal property and satisfy $\tau^2=1$, as checked on generators. Thus $(h\otimes1_D)(\tau s)=\tau((1_D\otimes h)s)=0$. The cited lemma with right factor $D$ gives $\tau s=0$, hence $s=0$. Its second application with right factor $L$ gives $t=0$. Therefore $r=(\iota\otimes\iota)t=0$, so $\Delta_C(x)=x\otimes g+g\otimes x$. Together with step 1, this is every required conclusion.
